name: Mont-Saint-Michel
about: The Bay of Mont-Saint-Michel at the turn of the tide: the Mount and Tombelaine on the flats, the salt meadows, the Couesnon and the Sée-Sélune channels, the Carolles cliffs to the north. 3 units a metre, true heights. Built by uv run 3d/mont-saint-michel-to-glb.py src/locations/mont-saint-michel.json assets/locations, which writes the terrain, the Mount and the bay texture

tide.about: Metres above mean sea level and seconds: a spring tide of 14 m, compressed into a cycle the viewer can watch; the flood takes `flood` of it, so the sea comes in faster than it goes out

bay.about: How the flats are made, the DEM having them all at sea level: `shore` metres high at the edge of the land, falling to `low` `reach` metres out (a curve of power `steepness`); land is lifted by `landLift` and kept at least `meadow` high, so the salt meadows are only reached by the creeks at high water. Channels follow OpenStreetMap's rivers, `channelDepth` deep and `channelWidth` wide, with `braids` thinner threads wandering either side

mount.about: The Mount, built from OpenStreetMap's walls, towers and houses on a granite rock rising from `sand` to `summit` metres under the abbey church, whose floor is at `floor` and whose spire carries Saint Michael's statue to `spire`

tombelaine.about: The granite islet 2.7 km north of the Mount: an ellipse `length` by `width` metres, its long side turned `heading` degrees from east, `height` metres high

walkers.about: A guided crossing on foot from Genêts to the Mount by way of Tombelaine, out on the sand whenever the tide leaves it dry; [lat, lon]

sheep.about: Salt meadow sheep: `flocks` flocks of up to `perFlock` on the meadows within `within` metres of the Mount

carolles.name: Carolles cliffs, a paragliding site over the bay

genets.name: Genêts, where the walks across the bay start

soaringLoop.about: Paramotors circle the Mount and its spire, low over the flats on the south-west and up past the statue's height on the north-east; [lat, lon, metres above sea level]

camera.about: Out over the flats south-east of the Mount, a little above the ramparts, looking north-west at the village and the abbey against the low sun; it circles the Mount once every `orbit` seconds; [lat, lon, metres]

look.about: Golden hour: the sun low in the west rakes the granite, a warm haze over the sea, less flat ambient light so the shade reads
